name: Petoi Quaddle
description: Petoi's cheapest, simplest quadruped — a single servo per leg (versus Bittle X's roughly nine) with wheels built directly into the foot tips, confirmed by Petoi's own founder, trading true lifted-paw walking for a rolling/gliding gait. Currently an active Kickstarter campaign, not yet shipping or available at retail.

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: Builder/Buddy 170–180g, Scout 198g — per press spec sheet (CNX Software); pre-shipping/provisional

specs.label: Dimensions
specs.note: Scout is taller (11cm) for its radar-head servo — per press spec sheet; provisional

specs.label: Compute
specs.note: cheaper/simpler than Bittle X's Biboard; optional AI Core or Pi Zero add-on

specs.label: Display
specs.note: press sources conflict on OLED vs. "color display" — unresolved

specs.label: Servos
specs.note: vs. Bittle X's ~9 — a single-motor linkage per leg, not two

specs.label: Feet
specs.note: confirmed by Petoi's founder — glides/rolls rather than walks like Bittle X

specs.label: Sensor
specs.note: human/motion detection; not an ultrasonic distance sensor

specs.label: Body
specs.note: snaps onto standard bricks; structural vs. cosmetic depth unconfirmed

specs.label: Tiers
specs.note: Buddy/Scout add AI Core voice chat; Scout adds dual IR distance sensors

sourcing: Specs compiled from Petoi's own Kickstarter and product pages, plus independent coverage from Hackster, Make:, and CNX Software, as of this build — Quaddle is still an active crowdfunding campaign, and final specs, pricing, and delivery timing may change before units ship.

pricing.summary: Reported early-bird pricing runs roughly $99–149 for the base "Builder" tier, $139–219 for "Buddy," and $179–269 for "Scout," with Petoi's own listed MSRP figures at $149 / $219 / $269. Quaddle is still funding on Kickstarter, so treat any of these figures as provisional until the campaign closes and units actually ship.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Quaddle runs on Petoi's open, MIT-licensed [OpenCat framework](https://github.com/PetoiCamp/OpenCat), but at Kickstarter launch its own firmware and hardware files hadn't yet been published — Petoi says it intends to open-source them before shipping, so no Open Source badge applies yet.
